div.div: Any check that fails stops here — the request is rejected, the app gets the error, and the attempt is still logged. A blocked call is evidence, not a gap in the record.

div.b: What this pipeline does not do

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 741px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
PII detection and content moderation are deliberately not gateway
guardrails. They belong to AI Runtime, which brings advanced DLP and
threat detection. If the customer needs inline scanning for prompt
injection, data leakage, or malicious content, the gateway alone does
not cover it — pair it with AIRS API Intercept.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 741px; margin-left: 683px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
It does not see traffic that does not come to it. Every check above
starts with a request that was addressed to the gateway. An application
still pointing at the provider endpoint passes through none of these
gates and appears in none of these logs. Coverage is an application
inventory exercise, and it is the part customers underestimate.
